speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly how many days the fever has lasted, and did the seizure occur before, during, or after the rash appeared? Also, have you recently traveled anywhere or been bitten by any insects?

speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text: The infant's immunization status is crucial, so can you confirm she has received the first dose of the MMR vaccine? Additionally, did the fever resolve completely before the rash appeared two days ago?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The MMR vaccine is not yet due at nine months, so the timing rules out measles. Since the fever broke before the rash appeared, this clinical picture strongly suggests roseola infantum.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Roseola Infantum (Exanthem Subitum)
